/Issued 858 PM MDT Thu Aug 20 2026/ 

 - Meteorological Overview:

Montana continues to be under the influence of an upper level 
ridge today, creating another day of warm temperatures and dry 
conditions. While these warm temperatures will last through 
Sunday, shortwaves embedded in the upper level ridge and an 
increase in monsoonal moisture will bring chances for showers and 
thunderstorms tomorrow through the weekend. Thunderstorms will 
mainly impact Southwest MT tomorrow night, with a transition to 
more stratiform precipitation Saturday morning. Saturday evening 
will see chances for thunderstorms in Southwest and Central MT, 
although isolated convection may make its way up to the Hi-Line. 
Sunday afternoon into the evening, thunderstorm chances increase 
to include Southwest, Central and North-Central MT. The main 
threat with these thunderstorms will be gusty winds, small hail, 
frequent lightning and brief, heavy downpours. While conditions 
are currently not favorable for strong to severe storms this 
weekend, we cannot rule out the possibility of an isolated one 
forming. 

The upper level ridge will begin to break down on Sunday as an 
upper level trough moves over the Northern Rockies from the west. 
This will bring breezy conditions across the CWA on Sunday. A cold
front moving through Sunday night will decrease temperatures to 
below seasonal averages Monday and Tuesday. However, another upper
level ridge building over Montana will cause temperatures to rise
again on Wednesday. This rise in temperatures will be short lived
as an upper level trough moves west once again, lowering 
temperatures and bringing back chances for showers and 
thunderstorms. -Dzomba


 - Forecast Confidence & Scenarios:

The main source of uncertainty in this forecast is the timing of 
the ridge break down and subsequent cold front. This timing will 
determine when we see the highest non-convective winds. Currently,
models are showing the ridge beginning to break down Sunday 
afternoon, which coincide with the peak of the breezy conditions.
If this ridge break down and cold front arrive earlier or later, 
the timing of the gusty winds will follow suit.

Thunderstorms:
There is a 15-20% chance of thunderstorms in Southwest MT tomorrow
night into early Saturday morning. On Saturday, there is a 25-30%
chance of thunderstorms in Southwest MT, and a 15-20% chance of
thunderstorms in Central MT. North-Central MT will see low, but
non-zero, chances of thunderstorms Saturday, generally below 15%.
On Sunday, there is a 25-40% chance of thunderstorms in Southwest
and Central MT, and a 15-20% chance of thunderstorms in North-Central
MT. Over the weekend. The inflow of monsoonal moisture will 
increase precipitable water to over an inch, creating the risk of 
localized flash flooding over burn scars with a stronger 
thunderstorm. The potential for flash flooding will depend on how 
fast the thunderstorm is moving, and what the rainfall rates 
associated with it are. 

Precipitation:
Saturday through Sunday, there is a 50-70% chance of at least a
wetting rain (0.1 inches) in Southwest MT. This chance decreases
to a 15-30% chance in Central MT, and a 5-15% chance in North-Central
MT. For a quarter of an inch during this same time period, there 
is a 15-25% chance in the valleys and a 35-50% chance in the 
mountains of Southwest MT. This chance decreases to less than 5% 
across Central and North-Central MT. 

Wind:
On Saturday, there is a greater than 50% chance for wind gusts 
greater than 25 mph throughout the CWA. For wind gusts greater 
than 30 mph, this chance remains greater than 50% east of a line 
between Havre and Lewistown, and south of Dillon. For the rest of 
the CWA, this chance decreases to 20-45%. For wind gusts greater 
than 40 mph, the only considerable chance will be in northern 
Blaine County, with a 50-75% chance. 

On Sunday, there is a greater than 75% chance of wind gusts 
greater than 25 mph across the entire CWA. For wind gusts greater 
than 30 mph, there is a 65-85% chance in Southwest MT, a 50-80% 
chance in Central MT, and a 45-65% chance in North-Central MT, 
with the exception of northern Blaine County and along the Rocky 
Mountain front, in which chances are 80-100%. For wind gusts 
greater than 40 mph, these chances decrease to 25-50% in 
Southwest MT, 15-30% in Central MT, 15-30% along the Hi-Line east 
of Chester, 20-50% along the Hi-Line west of Chester to Cut Bank, 
and 50-70% along the Rocky Mountain front. There is a 25-50% 
chance of wind gusts greater than 50 mph along the Rocky Mountain 
front. -Dzomba
